content:
Selective Availability changed GPS in two distinct steps.

The feature deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. In May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, the US government stopped using it to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

That was an operational change. In September 2007, the government announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability.

The 2007 announcement wasn’t the switch-off. It carried the 2000 policy into a future generation by specifying that the feature would be left out of GPS III.
